content: Do not operate machinery or engage in activities requiring alertness until you are certain you can do so safely. Avoid consuming alcoholic beverages. In children taking efavirenz, rashes may occur more frequently and can be more severe. Report any rash immediately to your healthcare provider. Your doctor may prescribe an antihistamine for your child to take before starting efavirenz to reduce the risk of rash. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary. Efavirenz may be part of a treatment plan to reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, this medication can pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor about breastfeeding while on this medication. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a detailed list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect how efavirenz is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Similarly, efavirenz can accelerate the removal of many other drugs from your body, which may impact their effectiveness. Certain HIV medications, such as elvitegravir, etravirine, nevirapine, or rilpivirine, may interact with efavirenz. If you are taking atazanavir with efavirenz, you may also need to take ritonavir to maintain effectiveness. Efavirenz may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to unintended pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use additional reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. Check the labels of all your medications, including allergy or cough-and-cold products, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine cannabinoid tests, potentially leading to false results. Inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel that you are taking efavirenz. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. Before starting efavirenz and while taking it, you should undergo laboratory and medical tests, such as liver function tests, viral load measurements, T-cell counts, and cholesterol and triglyceride levels. Keep all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments to monitor your condition and response to treatment. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used in combination with other HIV medications to help control HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. This reduces the risk of HIV-related complications, such as new infections or cancer, and improves your quality of life. However, efavirenz is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, continue taking all HIV medications exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as directed by your doctor. Do not share personal items, such as needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors, that may have come into contact with blood or other body fluids. Take this medication by mouth on an empty stomach, usually once daily at bedtime, as directed by your doctor. Taking efavirenz with food increases its blood levels, which may raise the risk of certain side effects. Swallow the medication whole with water. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, it can be opened, and the contents mixed gently with a small amount (1 to 2 teaspoons) of soft food, such as applesauce, grape jelly, or yogurt. After taking the mixed medication, add 2 more teaspoons of food to the empty mixing container and swallow the remaining mixture to ensure you receive the full dose. Consume the mixture within 30 minutes of preparation. Do not eat any food for 2 hours after taking this medication. For infants who cannot eat solid foods, the capsule contents may be mixed with 2 teaspoons of infant formula and drawn into an oral syringe for administration. Refer to the Patient Information Leaflet for detailed instructions. The dosage is based on your medical condition, response to treatment, and other medications you may be taking. For children, the dosage is also determined by weight. It is crucial to take this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. Do not skip doses, increase your dose, take it more frequently than prescribed, or stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. Common side effects include dizziness, difficulty sleeping, drowsiness, unusual dreams, and trouble concentrating. These side effects often begin 1 to 2 days after starting the medication and usually resolve within 2 to 4 weeks. Taking efavirenz on an empty stomach at bedtime can help reduce these effects. Avoid alcohol and recreational drugs while taking efavirenz. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. These reactions can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Changes in body fat distribution may occur while taking this medication, such as increased fat in the upper back and stomach areas and decreased fat in the arms and legs. The cause and long-term effects of these changes are unknown. Efavirenz commonly causes a rash, which is usually not serious. In adults, a rash may appear within the first 2 weeks of treatment and typically resolves within 4 weeks if it is not severe. In children, a rash may occur within the first 4 weeks of treatment. However, it may be difficult to distinguish a common rash from a rare rash that could indicate a severe reaction. Report any rash to your doctor immediately. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before taking efavirenz, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Efavirenz may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or if you have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This drug may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or difficulty concentrating. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Do not drive, operate machinery, or perform tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages.
